evidence: Highly organized directory structure with semantically grouped modules (cache, Downloaders, helpers, Misery, plugins)
Packages are logically cohesive with clear responsibilities (e.g., helpers for utilities/filters/decorators, Downloaders for external service integration)
Strong interdependence: modules import from multiple other modules (e.g., helpers/admins imports from cache/admins, Misery files import from helpers and config)
No evidence of process boundaries or network communication (no service discovery, RPC, or REST clients)
Single entry point (__main__.py) orchestrating the application
Shared domain model via config.py and centralized use of pyrogram/pytgcalls libraries
Fan-out is low to moderate (avg_fan_out=2.1), consistent with cohesive modules
No external interfaces defined (e.g., abstract ports), ruling out hexagonal
risks: Tight coupling between modules (e.g., helpers/admins depending directly on cache/admins) may hinder future refactoring or testing
Monolithic scaling limitations if load increases significantly
Potential for uncontrolled dependency cycles as the codebase grows (e.g., Misery modules import both helpers and plugins, creating feedback loops)
Lack of clear interface boundaries makes it harder to replace components (e.g., changing video downloader service)
